items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1976-02-04
items.q: Uh, Ricard Alexis and, uh, Moeys Durant sat in with Manuel, Manuel Perez.

ctx.x: some people have indicated that he really wanted Louis to stay with him in Chicago when Louis left and went to New York, and that I think Lil Armstrong, his wife, his second wife, sort of had an influence on his leaving the band. Do you think there was any bitterness on Joe's part when Louis left to go to Chicago?

Oh, that's not no bitterness. I don't think there was no, there was no bitterness, but it was a sort of a, a loss to Joe because there was a tradition in New Orleans to have two trumpets in the band. Papa Celestine had two, at one time, Manny Perez had two, first and second trumpet. And, uh, other bands around had two trumpets, and you played second. And it was guys, it's just like baseball, a second string catcher, you dig, more than one pitcher, and, uh, or more than one quarterback in a, a football team. It…

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Ricard Alexis was a hell of a trumpet player before they broke his jaw in a fight.

ctx.x: . . . with a gun and stuff, and he smashed . . . All the musicians ran. Jumped out the window, and he smashed all the instruments. Bunk’s trumpet was on the chair or something, and it got smashed up. Let me ask you this, Mr. Barker. You . . . Who were some of the better that you heard in New Orleans before you, before the ’20s, before you were a kid? Like some of the better clarinet players and trombone players.

There was a gang of them. Adolphe Alexander played the [expletive deleted] out the clarinet, but he never was featured. Hell of a musician. There was Alexander’s family. He had two brothers. One played drums. One played piano. The old man played baritone horn with my grandfather in the Onward Brass Band. There was Chris Kelly, a great trumpet player. It was funky. Had a following. A lot of people liked his music. At night he played a funky blues, nine different blues in nine different tempos. He played yard…
Did he end up playing bass?
